findings.description: The requirement mandates window-watchdog refresh while every supervised task is healthy, including when a non-task fault such as a code-integrity fault has been detected. SYS-SUP-010 and CON-SUP-121 prohibit watchdog servicing from fault detection until reset.
findings.requested_change: Qualify the refresh obligation so it does not apply after a fault has been detected.

findings.description: The requirement mandates independent-watchdog servicing while every supervised task is healthy, including when a non-task fault has been detected. SYS-SUP-010 and CON-SUP-121 prohibit watchdog servicing from fault detection until reset.
findings.requested_change: Qualify the servicing obligation so it does not apply after a fault has been detected.

findings.description: The requirement gives no deadline for sending the reset-cause message after classification. A verifier observing that no message has arrived cannot determine when the requirement has failed. OP-SYS-001 defers this missing limit even though it is needed to verify the obligation.
findings.requested_change: Classify OP-SYS-001 as blocking and obtain an observable deadline for the start-up message.

findings.description: The default task set, release order, start limits and execution limits are independently judgeable: for example, the task set can be correct while an execution limit is wrong.
findings.requested_change: Separate the independently verifiable default configuration obligations or reference a controlled configuration table whose entries can be judged independently.

findings.description: The answer deadline, selection and ordering of reports, END termination, empty-history response and replacement of the oldest stored report can fail independently, but are combined in one obligation.
findings.requested_change: Separate the response timing, response content and history replacement obligations into independently verifiable requirements.
